description: General, language-agnostic rules for interpreting data lineage and the edge cases that static parsers cannot resolve. Always supplied to the agents as grounding context.

rules.rule: Only assert lineage that is supported by the provided code snippet. Never invent table or column names. If a name is not in the evidence, do not output it.

Dynamic SQL, macro-injected code, and code read from a table at runtime cannot be resolved statically. Mark the upstream table as the source, state the assumption, and set low confidence rather than guessing the generated columns.
Runtime-bound function/method calls (e.g. getattr, reflection, string-built paths) should be reported as 'unresolved target' with the most likely candidate and an explicit assumption.

Cross-system handoffs (file export/import, DB links, API payloads) are legitimate lineage edges. A dataset written to a file and later read by another job forms one continuous chain through the file node.

When a step reads and writes the same dataset name, it is an in-place transformation. Record it as a self-update (or chain version) rather than a self-loop; the output columns may differ from the input.
Confidence: 0.9-1.0 explicit SQL/exports; 0.6-0.8 DATA-step merges/joins with clear keys; 0.3-0.5 dynamic/macro/runtime-resolved; <0.3 pure speculation (avoid).
For joins/merges, capture the join key(s) as part of the evidence; they justify the edge and support column-level lineage.

The glossary only defines what a name MEANS, to help read the code. It is never evidence of a data flow. Never propose or justify an edge because two terms are related in business meaning — every edge must come from the code snippet. If a glossary term is not present in the evidence, ignore it.
